predecessors.note: The Sultanate of 1856-1890 is the earlier dossier people-s-republic-of-zanzibar (Cliopatria's 'People's Republic of Zanzibar' row, 1856-1889); Cliopatria has no row for the protectorate years 1890-1963, and this row, 1963-1966, is the same sultanate again. The page says the UK 'did not grant Zanzibar independence, as such, because the UK never had sovereignty over Zanzibar'.

successors.note: 12 January 1964: after the revolution 'The country was renamed the People's Republic of Zanzibar and Pemba' (Zanzibar Revolution page); the Coastal Strip had gone to Kenya on 12 December 1963.
'In April 1964, the existence of this socialist republic was ended with its union with Tanganyika' (via the People's Republic; Cliopatria adds Zanzibar to its Tanzania shape only in 1967).

correction.text: the Zanzibar Archipelago, Unguja and Pemba, and only for 10 December 1963 to 12 January 1964 (the 16 km Kenyan coastal strip is in the found and loss events, two days apart); from 12 January 1964 the same land is the People's Republic of Zanzibar and Pemba, and from April 1964 part of Tanzania

keyframe_review.note: Three faults in Cliopatria's 1963-1966 row. (1) Years: the Sultanate ended on 12 January 1964 ('Jamshid bin Abdullah, the last sultan, was deposed and lost sovereignty over Zanzibar, marking the end of the Sultanate') and the islands joined Tanganyika in April 1964, yet the row runs to 1966 and Cliopatria's Tanzania shape grows by 4,189 km2 (882,278 to 886,467 km2) only in 1967. (2) Extent: the shape's bounding box reaches 8.0 S, south of the project gazetteer's Zanzibar region (6.4 S to 5.0 S), and its 4,245 km2 is larger than the archipelago the page describes; the page gives no area, so no infobox comparison is possible. (3) The 16 km coastal strip that the page puts in the Sultan's state was not in the shape and went to Kenya on 12 December 1963.

ledger.note: 10 December 1963: the British protectorate ends and the Sultan of Zanzibar rules a sovereign state. 'On 10 December 1963, the Protectorate that had existed over Zanzibar since 1890 was terminated by the United Kingdom.' The coastal strip is a researcher's reading of Coast Province and leaves two days later.

region.text: 'a 16-kilometre-wide (10 mi) strip along the Kenyan coast'; Coast Province is a coarse proxy for it

ledger.note: 12 December 1963: the Sultan's coastal strip becomes part of Kenya. 'the Sultan agreed that simultaneously with independence for Kenya, the Sultan would cease to have sovereignty over the Protectorate of Kenya'; the footnote on the 8 October 1963 agreement: 'the territories composing the Kenya Coastal Strip would become part of Kenya proper'. Kenya's independence day (12 December 1963) is on the Kenya page.

12 January 1964: the revolution ends the Sultanate. 'The revolution began on 12 January 1964 and led to the overthrow of the Sultan of Zanzibar Jamshid bin Abdullah and his mainly Arab government'; he and the prime minister 'fled the island on the royal yacht Seyyid Khalifa'. The Sultanate page: 'revolutionaries led by the African Afro-Shirazi Party overthrew the mainly Arab government'.

wars.name: Zanzibar Revolution
wars.outcome: The Sultan was deposed on 12 January 1964 and the country renamed the People's Republic of Zanzibar and Pemba; 'the UK did not intervene in the island's unrest' and the page does not say that any territory changed hands.
wars.note: The union with Tanganyika followed in April 1964 (the page gives both 23 April and 26 April).

certainty.note: Island coastlines; the Kenyan coastal strip was fixed by the agreement of 8 October 1963 and ceded on 12 December 1963.

sources.title: Sultanate of Zanzibar

sources.title: Zanzibar Revolution
sources.note: The revolution of 12 January 1964, the People's Republic of Zanzibar and Pemba, no British intervention, the territory (Unguja, Pemba), the union dates.

notes: Cliopatria's Sultanate of Zanzibar (1963-1966) is wrong in years: the state lasted from 10 December 1963 to 12 January 1964; the same islands were the People's Republic of Zanzibar and Pemba until the April 1964 union with Tanganyika (the Zanzibar Revolution page gives 23 April and 26 April), and part of Tanzania after that; the Tanzania dossier should include Zanzibar from April 1964, not from 1967 as Cliopatria does. The successor People's Republic needed a dossier (written here as people-s-republic-of-zanzibar-and-pemba). The earlier sultanate is the dossier people-s-republic-of-zanzibar (1856-1890, Cliopatria's 1856-1889 row), which is the same sultanate; the protectorate years 1890-1963 have no row. British colonial empire is named as the predecessor because the protectorate (not a sovereignty) ended on 10 December 1963. Family 'near-east' matches the earlier dossier. Pages: the Sultanate and Revolution pages (2, within budget). The Cliopatria shape's southern extent (to 8.0 S) is unexplained; the pages do not mention Mafia or any island south of Unguja.
